stem: On a supine abdominal X-ray, lucency outlines the falciform ligament; what is the best interpretation?

options.text: Football sign, suggesting free intraperitoneal gas
Sail sign, suggesting a normal thymus
Round pneumonia, suggesting focal lung consolidation
AP magnification of the heart and mediastinum

explanation: Football sign is the correct interpretation. On a supine abdominal X-ray, lucency outlining the falciform ligament indicates free intraperitoneal gas.

citations.source: Louisa Leone MD3 2025 - Child and Adolescent Health - Study Notes.pdf
citations.title: Louisa Leone MD3 2025 - Child and Adolescent Health - Study Notes.pdf

rationale: The falciform ligament can be outlined by free air on a supine abdominal X-ray, producing the football sign. This is an important radiographic sign of pneumoperitoneum.

optionExplanations.A: Correct because the football sign is caused by free intraperitoneal gas outlining the falciform ligament on a supine abdominal X-ray.
optionExplanations.B: Incorrect because the sail sign refers to the thymus on chest radiography and is not a falciform ligament finding on an abdominal X-ray.
optionExplanations.C: Incorrect because atelectasis is a chest radiograph finding and does not describe free gas outlining the falciform ligament.
optionExplanations.D: Incorrect because round pneumonia is a focal pulmonary consolidation, not a sign seen on supine abdominal X-ray.
optionExplanations.E: Incorrect because AP magnification affects apparent cardiac and mediastinal size on chest X-ray, not lucency around the falciform ligament.
